title: Why fast (Matthew 6:16–18)
hookLine: Jesus says when you fast, not if: quietly, without a gloomy face

cards: Skipping lunch is easy to announce. "Oh, I'm not eating today." A little sigh.
A small pause, in case anyone asks why. Some people do their diet or their detox out loud. Now go to Jesus on a hillside in Galilee, teaching a crowd.
He gets to fasting and doesn't explain it. He assumes it. Not if you fast.
When. Then he goes straight for the performance: people who look hungry on purpose, faces smudged and gloomy, so everyone can tell how holy they are. Do the opposite, he says.

teach.b: Fasting means going without food, or some food, for a time, for the sake of prayer.
In Matthew six, in the King James Bible: "Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast."
Then: "But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face; That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret."
Look normal: the same pattern as giving in secret a few lines earlier.
Of those who fast for show, Jesus says: "They have their reward." Jesus himself fasted: before his ministry began, the gospels say he spent forty days in the wilderness and was hungry afterward.
Moses fasted on the mountain. Elijah walked forty days on the strength of one meal. Esther asked her people to fast before she risked her life.
Jesus stands inside that tradition. Why choose hunger? Christians give a few reasons.
Hunger clears the head; it reminds you that you're a body, dependent, not in control.
Every pang becomes a small bell calling you back to prayer: hunger can pray. Fasting also makes room: the time and money you'd spend on food can go to someone else.
And it's a way of saying, with your whole body, that you mean it. A caution many churches give: fasting is not a diet, and it's not for everyone.
People who are pregnant, ill or recovering from an eating disorder are usually told not to fast from food at all. Many choose to fast from something else instead.

how: Many Christians fast by skipping meals or certain foods on set days or seasons, spending the time in prayer, and many give up a comfort instead when fasting from food isn't safe for them.

o: a strict diet to clear toxins from the body
going without food for a time, for prayer
giving up all food as a punishment for sin

games.q: you're fasting today. a coworker offers you a donut. what does Matthew 6 point toward?
o: decline simply, with a normal face.
sigh and look hungry so they ask.
games.why: "anoint thine head, and wash thy face; that thou appear not unto men to fast." the fast is between you and God.

practice: Think of one small comfort you reach for without thinking, the second coffee, the snack at three, the scroll before bed, and pick one. Picture the moment later today when you reach for it and find a small ache instead.
If you pray, let that ache become a short prayer; if you don't, let it be a moment of noticing.

wordCard.voice: Fasting. Going without for a while, for the sake of prayer. Jesus says when, not if, and quietly, with a washed face.

orig.note: Greek: a fast, going without food.

carryVoice: Your line: hunger can pray. A small ache can point somewhere. Day one hundred forty-six, done.
